title: Street Law: A Course in Practical Law
edition: School ISBN is the 8th-edition (2009) student workbook; outline taken from the 2021 student edition's TOC

sources.what: publisher table of contents for the 2021 edition (units, chapters, and sections)
Bookshare record for the 8th edition (Glencoe/McGraw-Hill, 2010, Arbetman and O'Brien)

summary: A practical-law course from Street Law, Inc. that teaches students how the legal system works and how law touches daily life, through case studies, mock trials, and 'You Be the Judge' problems. It covers the legal system, criminal and juvenile justice, torts, consumer law, family law, individual rights, and current legal issues.

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: Introduction to Law and the Legal System
toc.covers: What law is, how it is made and changed, how disputes are settled, and how courts and lawyers work.

children.label: Chapter 1
children.title: What Is Law?
children.covers: Law and values, human rights, the rule of law, balancing rights with responsibilities, kinds of laws, and the constitutional framework.

children.label: Chapter 2
children.title: Lawmaking
children.covers: How legislatures, agencies, and courts make law, and international lawmaking.

children.label: Chapter 3
children.title: Advocacy
children.covers: Advocating for change through lobbying, voting, and campaign finance rules.

children.label: Chapter 4
children.title: Settling Disputes
children.covers: Methods of resolving disputes outside court, such as negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.

children.label: Chapter 5
children.title: The Court System
children.covers: Trial and appeals courts, state and federal systems, tribal and military courts, the U.S. Supreme Court, and international courts.

children.label: Chapter 6
children.title: Lawyers
children.covers: When you need a lawyer, how to find one, and how people become lawyers.

toc.label: Unit 2
toc.title: Criminal Law and Juvenile Justice
toc.covers: Crime and its causes, criminal offences and defences, the criminal justice process from arrest to corrections, and the juvenile system.

children.label: Chapter 7
children.title: Crime in America
children.covers: The nature of crime, campus crime, gangs, guns and the law, substance abuse, victims, and crime prevention and reporting.

children.label: Chapter 8
children.title: Introduction to Criminal Law
children.covers: State and federal crimes, felonies and misdemeanours, parties to crimes, crimes of omission, and attempt, solicitation, and conspiracy.

children.label: Chapter 9
children.title: Crimes Against the Person
children.covers: Homicide, suicide, kidnapping, assault and battery, and rape and sexual assault.

children.label: Chapter 10
children.title: Crimes Against Property
children.covers: Arson, vandalism, larceny, embezzlement, robbery, extortion, burglary, forgery, receiving stolen property, vehicle misuse, and cybercrime.

children.label: Chapter 11
children.title: Defenses
children.covers: Defences claiming no crime occurred, mistaken identity, justification or excuse such as self-defence, and lack of criminal responsibility such as insanity.

children.label: Chapter 12
children.title: Criminal Justice Process: The Investigative Phase
children.covers: Arrest, search and seizure under the Fourth Amendment, and interrogations and confessions (Miranda).

children.label: Chapter 13
children.title: Criminal Justice Process: Proceedings Before Trial
children.covers: Booking, bail, preliminary hearings, grand juries, arraignment and pleas, pretrial motions, and plea bargaining.

children.label: Chapter 14
children.title: Criminal Justice Process: The Trial
children.covers: Jury trial, speedy and public trial, confronting witnesses, self-incrimination, right to counsel, and appeals.

children.label: Chapter 15
children.title: Criminal Justice Process: Sentencing and Corrections
children.covers: Sentencing options, purposes of punishment, parole, capital punishment, and prisons and inmate rights.

children.label: Chapter 16
children.title: Juvenile Justice
children.covers: History of juvenile courts, status offences, how juvenile cases proceed today, and current challenges.

toc.label: Unit 3
toc.title: Torts
toc.covers: Civil wrongs and liability: intentional torts, negligence, strict liability, and tort reform.

children.label: Chapter 17
children.title: Torts: A Civil Wrong
children.covers: The idea of liability, types of torts, taking a case to court, and insurance.

children.label: Chapter 18
children.title: Intentional Torts
children.covers: Damages and torts that harm persons (such as battery and defamation) or property (such as trespass), and their defences.

children.label: Chapter 19
children.title: Negligence
children.covers: Duty, breach, causation, damages, and defences to negligence suits.

children.label: Chapter 20
children.title: Strict Liability
children.covers: Liability without fault for dangerous activities, animals, and defective products.

children.label: Chapter 21
children.title: Torts and Public Policy
children.covers: Debates over tort reform.

toc.label: Unit 4
toc.title: Consumer Law
toc.covers: Contracts, warranties, credit, deceptive sales, consumer protection, and major purchases such as cars, housing, and college.

children.label: Chapter 22
children.title: Contracts
children.covers: Elements of a contract, minors and contracts, written vs oral and illegal contracts, and breach.

children.label: Chapter 23
children.title: Warranties
children.covers: Express and implied warranties and disclaimers.

children.label: Chapter 24
children.title: Credit and Other Financial Services
children.covers: Bank accounts, how credit works and what it costs, credit applications and denials, and default and debt collection.

children.label: Chapter 25
children.title: Deceptive Sales Practice
children.covers: Telemarketing, door-to-door sales, advertising, bait and switch, online commerce, and repair estimates.

children.label: Chapter 26
children.title: Becoming a Smart Consumer
children.covers: Influences on consumers, consumer protection agencies and laws, and how to resolve complaints, including in court.

children.label: Chapter 27
children.title: Major Purchases
children.covers: Buying a car, renting a place to live, paying for college, and health care.

toc.label: Unit 5
toc.title: Family Law
toc.covers: Legal rules for families from marriage to divorce, parents and children, foster care and adoption, and government benefits.

children.label: Chapter 28
children.title: Law and the American Family
children.covers: How law affects people from birth to death and legal definitions of family.

children.label: Chapter 29
children.title: Marriage
children.covers: Getting married, legal and financial aspects of marriage, common-law marriage, intimate partner violence, unmarried couples, and the marriage equality cases.

children.label: Chapter 30
children.title: Parents and Children
children.covers: Parent-child responsibilities and child abuse and neglect.

children.label: Chapter 31
children.title: Foster Care and Adoption
children.covers: How foster care and adoption work.

children.label: Chapter 32
children.title: Separation, Divorce, and Custody
children.covers: Marriage problems, separation and divorce, child custody, alimony, property division, child support, and stepparents.

children.label: Chapter 33
children.title: Government Support for Families and Individuals
children.covers: Economic, health, and educational benefits programmes.

toc.label: Unit 6
toc.title: Individual Rights and Liberties
toc.covers: Constitutional rights: speech, press, religion, due process, privacy, and protection from discrimination.

children.label: Chapter 34
children.title: Introduction to Constitutional Law
children.covers: Constitutional amendments and basic principles of constitutional law.

children.label: Chapter 35
children.title: Freedom of Speech
children.covers: Why free speech matters and its limits: commercial speech, obscenity, defamation, fighting words, time-place-manner rules, symbolic speech, and vague laws.

children.label: Chapter 36
children.title: Freedom of the Press
children.covers: Prior restraint, press access to information, and compelled disclosure of sources.

children.label: Chapter 37
children.title: Expression in Special Places
children.covers: First Amendment rights in public schools, prisons, and the military.

children.label: Chapter 38
children.title: Freedom of Religion
children.covers: The Establishment Clause and the Free Exercise Clause.

children.label: Chapter 39
children.title: Due Process
children.covers: Procedural and substantive due process.

children.label: Chapter 40
children.title: The Right to Privacy
children.covers: Privacy at home and school, government and private information gathering, and reproductive rights.

children.label: Chapter 41
children.title: Discrimination
children.covers: Discrimination based on race, national origin and citizenship, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, age, and disability, plus housing discrimination and state and local laws.

toc.label: Unit 7
toc.title: Contemporary Issues in Law
toc.covers: Immigration, intellectual property, terrorism, workplace rights, and environmental law.

children.label: Chapter 42
children.title: Immigration Law
children.covers: Citizenship, visitors and permanent residents, refugees and asylum, undocumented immigrants, detention and removal, and immigration policy.

children.label: Chapter 43
children.title: Intellectual Property
children.covers: Patents, copyrights, and trademarks.

children.label: Chapter 44
children.title: Law and Terrorism
children.covers: Surveillance and searches, international terrorism law, and torture and detainee issues.

children.label: Chapter 45
children.title: Rights and Responsibilities in the Workplace
children.covers: Job seeking, conditions on the job, and losing a job.

children.label: Chapter 46
children.title: Environmental Law
children.covers: NEPA, the Clean Air and Clean Water Acts, the Endangered Species Act, land pollution, other federal laws, regulation at each level of government, and climate change.

notes: The school's ISBN (9780078895180) is the 8th-edition student workbook (2009), which goes with the 8th-edition text (Glencoe/McGraw-Hill, 2010). No 8th-edition TOC could be fetched, so this outline uses the 2021 edition. Expect differences: the 8th edition reportedly had six units with a 'Consumer and Housing Law' unit and no separate 'Contemporary Issues' unit, and chapter numbers will not line up. Treat Units 1-3 as the most stable. The 2021 TOC also lists section headings, which are summarised in each chapter's description rather than listed separately. Unit 5 and Chapters 40-41 cover marriage, sexuality, and reproductive-rights law and may need a teacher's framing.
